editorial:
Ever wonder what happens when the richest guys on Earth decide to race each other into the stars? You get a wild look at the ego and money behind the new space race. This documentary focuses on Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, and Richard Branson, showing how they all want to be the first to make space travel normal for everyone. It feels less like a dry school lesson and more like a high-stakes competition between billionaires who simply cannot stand to lose to one another. The vibe is fast and exciting, making you feel the tension as they build massive rockets and plan their big leaps into the unknown.

What really works here is the inside access provided by The Washington Post, giving you a peek behind the curtain at how these companies actually run. The pacing is snappy, though some parts feel a bit too focused on the money and not enough on the actual science. If you love business battles or space, you need to see this.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing that while these men have made huge leaps in tech, the race is far from over. It ends with a look at the different goals they have, from Musk wanting to live on Mars to Bezos focusing on space stations. There is no single winner, but the conclusion makes it clear that the real victory is that space is now open for private business, not just governments.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves space, business, or tech billionaires.
